locator: Aristotle, Categories, chapter10; Internet Classics Archive translation by E.M.Edghill; complete Part10 through before Part11
source_summary: Privation and possession concern an appropriate common bearer. Lack of a faculty counts as privation only when it should naturally be present; creatures lacking sight or teeth before that stage are not thereby called blind or toothless. This differs from plain assertion and denial. The complete chapter also distinguishes relatives and contraries.
